A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianFlowOcc. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Occ3D-nuScenes occupancy results, component ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v3 retains original occupancy experiments and adds depth-estimation results, fully supervised occupancy results and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a supervised adaptation using differentiable voxelization and voxel-label cross-entropy, without the Temporal Module or Gaussian Splatting supervision. The principal weakly supervised architecture remains unchanged; the new Temporal Propagation subsection clarifies an existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes/Occ3D-nuScenes for the same driving-scene coverage. Depth was already rendered, supervised and qualitatively evaluated in v1. v3 adds quantitative depth scoring and another occupancy supervision regime, without introducing a new dataset, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: The original occupancy comparator set is retained. New Table A.2 evaluates against SurroundDepth and SimpleOcc alongside OccNeRF, SelfOcc and GaussianOcc; Table A.3 introduces evaluated comparisons with BEVFormer, OccFormer, FB-Occ and CTF-Occ. Figure B.5 also adds a direct qualitative comparison with GaussianOcc.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a fully supervised experimental protocol using 3D voxel labels and explicitly omitting the camera visibility mask (Appendix A.3). Its depth benchmark adds seven depth metrics (Table A.2). The existing weakly supervised training settings remain stated as before; the PDFs do not establish a protocol change explaining the revised mIoUs.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds flow-versus-no-flow visualizations across three past and three future frames, extending the existing next-frame analysis. Appendix B.4 adds case studies of thin objects, object bleeding and shape reconstruction against GaussianOcc. The original quantitative ablation questions and configurations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or formal significance tests. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported full-model mIoU changes from 16.02 to 17.08, and the no-depth result from 13.20 to 14.07, with corresponding updates to ablations and relative gains. Table A.1's per-class scores remain unchanged; the new aggregates match their averages, so this does not establish improved predictions. New Tables A.2 and A.3 report depth results, including RMSE 5.232, and fully supervised occupancy at 25.28 mIoU, respectively.

T1.justification: The time-token definition changes from a T-by-D matrix to a 2T-by-D matrix, correcting its cardinality for T past and T future frames (v1 Section 3.5; v3 Section 3.6). The attention and voxelization mathematics otherwise remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: sparse Gaussian representation, efficient induced attention, weak supervision, learned temporal motion compensation and superior weakly supervised occupancy performance with approximately 50-fold faster inference. Merging contribution bullets does not alter their substance.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion of the depth-versus-occupancy accuracy tradeoff, acknowledges remaining errors in weakly learned flow, and attributes reduced object bleeding to long-term temporal consistency (Appendices A.2, B.3 and B.4). The existing limitations concerning RGB supervision and more sophisticated motion modeling remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v3 reports that code is available and directs readers to installation, training and evaluation instructions (Section 4.2 and Appendix D). Section 3.3 also explicitly describes recurrent memory with single-time-step inputs. The main hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly relates its sparse representation to GaussianFormer and GaussianWorld and expands discussion of driving-scene reconstruction and GaussianAD. Six references are added, including SurroundDepth, DrivingRecon, Street Gaussians and DrivingGaussian. This extends the existing positioning without redefining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: The main text receives localized language and notation edits, merges two contribution bullets, and moves the temporal-alignment explanation into a dedicated subsection with additional clarification. The appendix gains descriptive subsections and a source-code section; the overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The supplement substantially expands its displays with Tables A.2–A.3 and Figures B.2 and B.5. Existing depth and next-frame illustrations are retained as Figures B.3–B.4 and combined on one page. Figure 2 gains training/inference color coding, and Figure 3's labels and positional-encoding display are revised.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmarks and diagnostic figures make the method's applicability and limitations easier to assess. Clearer temporal-propagation documentation and reported code availability also improve reproducibility. These are useful extensions to an already developed paper, although the unexplained aggregate-mIoU revisions limit interpretation of the increased reported performance.
